parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no traveller-facing criminalisation or targeting: same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2022, no gender-expression statute is documented, soliciting prosecutions date to 1990–1994 (dead-letter enforcement), and prison data show trans inmates held without recorded assault. Strong rule of law means any incident has functioning recourse. No documented border, facility or care exposures for visitors — but no documented protections either; border screening practice is unresolved, and the state tolerates residual threat-framing (broadcast code grouping homosexuality with paedophilia), no LGBTI registration, and no gender-identity anti-discrimination cover. Conservative social climate with modest acceptance (58% accept family members). Sits just below the 0.75 tier: no documented harms, but no documented protective machinery and thin documentation of visitor-specific treatment.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; how checkpoint officers treat document/presentation mismatch is explicitly unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Unresolved question is an open issue, not a documented exposure; officer practice unknown at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. Section 294 (obscene acts, up to 3 months) exists but enforcement not disaggregated; soliciting charges date to 1990–1994.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Prison service reported 10 trans inmates, no recorded assaults (Nov 2023).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody outcomes would flow through functioning courts; no documented pattern of hostile application to trans people.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Gender-neutral toilet conversion drew boycott threats and petitions — social friction, not a facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Gender-neutral toilets exist at two university colleges; no facility restrictions documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Venue-level variation only; no official exclusion rule documented.

care_services.exposure: Stakeholder report documents discrimination and harassment in healthcare for residents; surgical-gated LGR is resident-facing.
care_services.protection: Health minister stated evidence-based practice and respect for patient preferences, with medical-council recourse (2020).
care_services.interaction: Resident-facing harms; visitor-facing care denial not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Broadcast code groups homosexuality with paedophilia/incest (2025); LGBTI organisations cannot register; media regulator restricts 'promotion' of homosexual lifestyles.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Repeal of 377A (2022); pride rally held annually since 2009 with ~28,000 attendees; gay venues operate openly; community felt safer per June 2023 report.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State tolerates expression rather than targeting it; no documented police action against trans people.

minors_guardians.exposure: School discrimination facing trans students is resident-facing; nothing reaches travelling minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling guardian faces the same open border-document question as solo adults.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data located; absence is not evidence of safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Strong rule of law; functioning police and courts; 80% youth survey acceptance of working with LGBTQ people.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Any public incident would have normal recourse channels.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity protection under the 2025 workplace-fairness law; no relationship recognition; border screening unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Medical-council complaints channel; functioning institutions throughout.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Gaps are resident-facing or open questions, not documented visitor exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-B documents actual border secondary screening and refusals of trans visitors; here no such friction is documented — only an unresolved question — so this jurisdiction sits above it.

0.75-C has documented respectful border training and appellate remedies; here protections are thinner and social/state climate more constrained (broadcast code, no registration), so this sits just below.
0.35-A features a universal visitor-exclusion register with routine enforcement; nothing comparable exists here — no traveller-facing restriction is documented at all, so this is far above that tier.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of decriminalisation without positive protection: no statute or enforcement practice reaches trans visitors, the sodomy repeal removed a latent lever, and custodial data show no abuse. What holds the score below the 0.75–0.85 tier is the absence of any documented protective machinery reaching visitors, unresolved border-screening practice for mismatched documents, residual state-level threat-framing in media regulation, and a socially conservative majority (only 58% accepting of LGBTQ family members) that poses friction rather than documented hostility. Unknowns are extrapolated toward moderate-low risk given strong rule of law, functioning institutions, and open pride expression, not toward neutrality.
